Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the Channel Islands of California — the defining cold-water surf region that produced Tom Curren, Kelly Slater training grounds, and a generation of shapers. Paired with Coast for an accessible compound. Counter to Greenough Spoon (too insider) and Leash Lab (overly tech-leaning).
Modern.industrySummary: Modern surf brands compete on shape vocabulary and regional identity rather than tropical-beach lifestyle. The opening is for a brand that names a specific cold-water coast and stays in the shaping-and-paddling register.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Outerknown (outerknown.com) plays the modern sustainability-led peer. Mollusk Surf Shop (mollusksurfshop.com) holds the editorial-design middle. Saturdays NYC (saturdaysnyc.com) is the urban surf reference. We sit alongside Mollusk with a sharper regional anchor.
Modern.positioningStatement: Channel & Coast is a modern cold-water surf brand making boards, wetsuits, and apparel for the California Channel Islands tradition.

targetAudience.primary: Surfers 25-45 who paddle out year-round in cold water and care about shape vocabulary.

dos: Name the shaper and the foam
Show the actual coast, not Bali
donts: Sell 'beach lifestyle' as the whole pitch

Modern.logoDirection: Wordmark: CHANNEL & COAST set in a confident modern grotesk, two words and an ampersand on one line. Small mark: a single channel-bottom board outline used on hangtags and the favicon.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for board specs and water temps
typography.rationale: A modern grotesk plus its mono — the shaper's-spec register.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Bells Beach, Australia — home of the Rip Curl Pro Bells Beach (the world's longest-running surf contest, since 1961), where the trophy is a literal cast bell. Bells is geographic; Brass evokes the trophy. Counter to Maison Kahanamoku (surname/estate flag) and Pipeline Atelier (Pipeline TM-crowded in surfwear).
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury surf is a small editorial category — heritage board craft, hand-stitched wetsuits, and contest-trophy register. Buyers pay for provenance and patina.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Almond Surfboards (almondsurfboards.com) plays the heritage-craft peer. Captain Fin Co (captainfinco.com) holds the editorial-design middle. Hodaddy (hodaddysurf.com) is the heritage reference. We sit as a contest-trophy heritage house.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Bells & Brass is a heritage surf house drawing on the Bells Beach contest tradition, with hand-shaped boards and trophy-grade craft.

targetAudience.primary: Surfers and collectors 35-65 who buy heritage boards and care about contest history.

dos: Name the shaper and the year
Treat the board as the artifact

Luxury.logoDirection: Wordmark: BELLS & BRASS set in a refined serif, two lines centered. A small mark — a single cast-bell silhouette — used as the seal.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Garamond Premier Pro for body and contest history
typography.rationale: Two classical English serifs — the heritage contest register.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Anchor: George Greenough's 1965 'spoon' kneeboard — the radical concave-bottom shape that triggered the shortboard revolution. Single word with a period for finality. Picked from Agent A's three for the deepest insider anchor.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimalist surf brands serve the shaping-literate market that wants the form and the foam, not the lifestyle scaffolding.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Album Surf (albumsurf.com) plays the modern-shape peer. Wegener Surfboards (wegenersurfboards.com) holds the shaping-craft middle. CJ Nelson Designs (cjnelsondesigns.com) is the editorial reference. We sit as a single-shape minimal brand.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Spoon. is a minimalist surf brand built on the 1965 Greenough spoon shape.

targetAudience.primary: Surfers 30-55 who read shaping history and own multiple boards.
behaviors: Care about board concave and rocker

dos: Name the foam and the glasser

Minimal.logoDirection: Wordmark: SPOON. set very large in a clean modern sans, one word with a period. No symbol.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for board specs
typography.rationale: Clean Diatype with its mono — the shaper's-spec register.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the California cold-water surf coast — Channel Islands, Point Conception, and the broader Pacific coast as a multi-brand operating region. Counter to Channel Islands Maritime Co. (Channel Islands Surfboards is an active brand) and Kahanamoku Surf Holdings (surname/estate flag) and Bramah Coast Group (Bramah TM conflict from locksmith industry).
Corporate.industrySummary: Multi-brand surf and water-sports operators are a quietly large B2B category — companies that own portfolios of board, wetsuit, and apparel brands and serve specialty surf retailers.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Boardriders (boardriders.com) plays the institutional multi-brand peer. Rip Curl (ripcurl.com) holds the brand reference. Hurley (hurley.com) is the corporate parent reference. We sit as a regional multi-brand operator.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Coast & Maritime Group operates a portfolio of surf, wetsuit, and water-sports brands with shared sourcing and retail distribution.

targetAudience.primary: Surf brand founders considering sale, specialty surf retail buyers, and institutional investors.
behaviors: Care about wetsuit sourcing and compliance

dos: Lead with brand portfolio and sourcing footprint
donts: No social media at the parent level

Corporate.logoDirection: Wordmark: COAST & MARITIME GROUP set in an institutional serif, three lines. A small mark — a coastline-and-wave silhouette — used on contracts.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and headlines
typography.rationale: A reading serif plus a clean grotesk — the boardroom register.

Creative.tagline: The revolution was a foot shorter.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the late-1960s shortboard revolution that overthrew the longboard establishment (Greenough, Nat Young, McTavish). 'Long Live Short' is a witty inversion that names the revolution in three words. Counter to Mickey & Malibu (Mickey Dora's family/estate concerns) and Greenough's Ghost (surname).
Creative.industrySummary: Creative surf brands play on shape vocabulary and surf history. The shortboard-vs-longboard tension is one of the sport's defining narratives and is editorially rich.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Captain Fin Co (captainfinco.com) plays the editorial-design peer. Mollusk Surf Shop (mollusksurfshop.com) holds the cultural middle. Sun Diego (sundiego.com) is the lifestyle reference. We sit as a shape-history-led brand.
Creative.positioningStatement: Long Live Short is a creative surf brand celebrating the shortboard revolution with editorial labels and shape-history apparel.

targetAudience.primary: Surfers 25-50 who read surf history and care about shape lineage.
behaviors: Read Drew Kampion and Matt Warshaw

dos: Print shape history on the label
Name the shaper and the year

Creative.logoDirection: Wordmark: LONG LIVE SHORT in a 1960s display sans, three words stacked. A small mark — a shortboard silhouette over a longboard outline — used on tags.

typography.primary: Druk for the wordmark and headlines
typography.rationale: A confident display sans plus a quiet grotesk — the 1968-poster register.
